jobs.title: Senior Director Enterprise Architecture & Ontology
jobs.description:
A career as a Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture & Ontology within the Enterprise Architecture team at National Bank means acting as the Senior Director responsible for Enterprise Architecture and Integrated Enterprise Knowledge. It means contributing to the definition and evolution of a strategic practice that provides a better understanding of the relationships between business capabilities, processes, data, applications, interfaces, technologies, and controls. This role allows you to make a positive impact on our organization through your expertise in enterprise architecture, semantic modelling, and organizational transformation supported by artificial intelligence and automation.

Your job

Shape
the evolution of the enterprise architecture practice by defining
directions, methods, standards, and priorities that support
decision-making and organizational transformation.

Define
and evolve an enterprise ontology that connects business capabilities,
processes, data, applications, interfaces, technology components, and
controls through clear semantics and governed relationships.

Establish
modelling principles, governance mechanisms, and accountabilities that
enable different teams to contribute to a shared, reliable, and reusable
understanding of the enterprise.

Leverage
artificial intelligence and automation to discover and reconcile
relationships across LeanIX, the CMDB, and other authoritative sources
without creating a new monolithic repository, while ensuring information
quality, governance, and traceability.

Transform
the enterprise ontology into products, views, integrations, and use cases
that support strategic planning, impact analysis, technology decisions,
and transformation initiatives.

Represent
the practice in architecture and delivery forums, engage stakeholders, and
measure adoption, coverage, and value delivered to adjust priorities based
on the organization’s needs.

Your team

The Enterprise Architecture practice brings together
specialists who work collaboratively to develop an integrated understanding of
the organization and support its transformation. You work closely with
architecture, business, data, technology, and platform teams.

Within the Enterprise Architecture sector, you report
to the Bank’s Chief Architect. You contribute to transforming knowledge that is
currently distributed across multiple teams, repositories, and tools into a
coherent, accessible, and actionable view that supports decision-making.

We aim to provide you with maximum flexibility to
enhance your quality of life. This includes a hybrid work environment as well
as a flexible and adaptable schedule.

The Bank values continuous development and internal
mobility. Our personalized training programs, based on learning through
experience, help you master your role and develop new areas of expertise.
Resources such as the Data Academy, language training, the Harvard Learning
Center, as well as coaching and mentoring support, are available to you at all
times.

Prerequisites

University
degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field and at least
ten years of relevant experience in enterprise or solution architecture.

In-depth
expertise in enterprise ontology, semantic modelling, or knowledge graphs,
as well as modelling relationships between business and technology assets.

Strong
command of enterprise architecture repositories and authoritative sources,
including LeanIX and CMDBs.

Expertise
in information governance, data quality, traceability, and the
reconciliation of data from multiple sources.

Hands-on
experience with artificial intelligence and automation applied to
relationship discovery, knowledge quality improvement, and the delivery of
enterprise capabilities.

Strong
understanding of integration architectures, application programming
interfaces (APIs), event-driven architectures, cloud computing, and
digital ecosystems.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to discuss frequently with our service providers or partners who speak a language other than French.
Required skills: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, Critical Thinking, Cross-functional Collaboration, Enterprise Architecture, Enterprise Integration, Influencing, Information Governance, Innovation Management, Knowledge Graph, Micro Focus UCMDB, Model Making, Ontologies, Semantics, Strategic Vision, Strategy Execution

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. We aim, wherever possible, to provide a barrier-free and accessible environment to all employees.

We strive to provide accessibility measures throughout the recruitment process within the limits of our available resources. If you require accommodations, feel free to let us know during our initial conversations. We welcome all candidates! What can you bring to our team?

Join us!

Together, the work we do connects people and changes lives — including your own.

Be part of a dynamic, collaborative and caring organization committed to saving and improving lives. Thousands of patients depend on us every day for reliable access to safe blood, plasma, stem cells and organs and tissues.

About The Role

Canadian Blood Services is seeking a Regular Full-Time Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization
to join our Enterprise Portfolio, Program and Project Management Office (ePMO)
team in our Ottawa or Toronto office.

The ePMO
team delivers programs and services that advance valuable organizational initiatives, ensuring they are completed on time and on budget. Our focus is on maximizing business outcomes for Canadian Blood Services and the people in Canada we serve.

As the Associate Director, Portfolio Governance and Value Realization, you will lead value realization and benefits tracking activities aligned with corporate strategy, corporate funding cycles, and the delivery of high-visibility projects and programs across the organization.

Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Program Enablement & Project Management Office, you will lead ePMO-led value realization activities across enterprise programs and provide guidance to support value-informed decision-making. You will contribute to enterprise portfolio management and reporting for all corporate priority projects, including ePMO projects; escalate issues requiring executive attention; and provide leadership to enterprise projects coordinated through process management. You will also ensure compliance with corporate portfolio reporting requirements and support the execution of select projects within the portfolio by fostering collaboration and integration across divisions. In addition, you will provide a challenge function across other ePMO activities, including reporting, automation and artificial intelligence (AI), data and analytics, and alignment with corporate strategy.

Formula for success

Leveraging your skills in ePMO operations, you will oversee value realization driven through programs, providing leadership, coordination, and management of enterprise PMO processes and functions.
Applying your expertise in value realization leadership, you will oversee the development of proposals and business cases, as required, to help articulate anticipated benefits and the value proposition.
Demonstrating your skills in influencing and negotiating, you will motivate and coach staff for high performance, act with transparency, and promote a problem-solving mindset and collaborative culture.
Utilizing your experience in benefits management and performance measurement, you will ensure all centrally delivered projects and programs have defined benefits, measured using key performance indicators, tracked, and communicated in a consistent and effective manner, and incorporate effective change and risk management controls.
Drawing on your skills in project interdependency management and prioritization, you will identify, manage, and address interdependencies between projects and prioritization to drive the greatest value.
Demonstrating your ability to lead with empathy and emotional intelligence, you will apply the advanced soft skills required to lead and motivate others to achieve deliverables, particularly when priorities and expectations may be in conflict.
Contributing your expertise in strategic initiatives and project leadership, you will take a lead role in developing and maintaining various initiatives and participate in special projects and corporate initiatives as assigned by the Director.
Applying your skills in performance improvement and governance, you will identify opportunities to improve performance and apply fit-for-purpose processes that balance governance and empowerment.
Fostering your strengths in people leadership and talent development, you will create a high-performing, engaged, and inclusive team environment by setting clear expectations, developing talent, supporting career growth and succession planning, and promoting continuous learning, collaboration, and professional development.
Applying your analytical and problem-solving skills, you will use your seasoned experience and knowledge to analyze highly complex problems, interpret business needs, and develop integrated, innovative solutions. This will often require deeper investigation of conflicting information and novel thinking to establish solutions.

Desired Education And Skills

A bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Science, Public Administration, Health Administration, or a related discipline. A master’s degree (MBA, MPA, MSc, or equivalent) is considered an asset. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience managing multiple projects and programs involving large teams, significant budgets, and multiple stakeholders, including at the executive level.
Demonstrated ability to build and lead teams, including managing, coaching, and developing project managers, employees, and contracted resources.
Proven ability to manage a significant project portfolio within a large organization, with a focus on value realization and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated success in establishing and maturing value-driven portfolios and programs that support organizational transformation and strategic objectives.
Expertise in process transformation and service delivery, including the ability to develop recommendations and present outcomes to executive leadership.
Strong analytical and technical capabilities, with the ability to leverage portfolio reporting, data analytics, performance metrics, automation, and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve decision-making, reporting, and operational efficiency.
Knowledge of corporate planning, budgeting, and financial management processes that support effective portfolio management and prioritization.
Familiarity with introducing new products or processes within a regulated environment is considered an asset.
Knowledge of managing and implementing process changes within a unionized workforce environment is considered an asset.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain project and portfolio documentation, reports, business cases, and executive-level presentations.
Familiarity with Agile methodologies and working within Agile teams is considered an asset.
Proficiency with relevant project and portfolio management tools, including Microsoft Project Professional and Microsoft Project Online (MSPO), is considered an asset.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, including collaboration, facilitation, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement.
Strong financial and operational planning capabilities, with the ability to align resources, budgets, and priorities with organizational objectives.

What We Offer You

4 weeks’ vacation.
Comprehensive group health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family.
Annual performance award of up to 10%.
Defined benefit pension plan.
Employee discounts, wellness programs, and access to professional development resources.

What You Can Expect

This role requires a minimum of 40% on-site presence at 1800 Alta Vista Drive, Ottawa, Ontario or 67 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Additional on-site work may be required based on business needs. On-site expectations are subject to change and may be adjusted on a temporary or permanent basis.
You will work Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week, 7.5 hours per day.
Travel is required to attend meetings and to fulfill project commitments.

If this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply by providing your up-to-date resume. This could be your first step towards a meaningful and inspiring career. Come to work each day knowing that you save lives.

We acknowledge that the work of Canadian Blood Services spans many Territories and Treaty areas across the country, and we are grateful for the Traditional Knowledge Keepers and Elders who have guided us in this important work. We recognize the land and waters that have inspired our work and offer gratitude to those Indigenous peoples on whose territory we work, live and play.

Diversity and inclusion play a vital role in ensuring health equity for patients across Canada. We are committed to reflecting Canada’s population in our organization and fostering an environment where all employees can be their authentic selves, with equal opportunities to succeed and contribute.

We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those considered for an interview or those invited to participate in an assessment will be contacted. Emails are sent directly from our system, to ensure you receive them please add donotreply@blood.ca and system@successfactors.com to your safe senders list.

Applicants who require accommodation should discuss their needs with us.

jobs.title: Director - Policy & Planning, Integrated Acute & Episodic Care
jobs.description:
Director - Policy & Planning, Integrated Acute & Episodic Care

Req ID: 228590

Location: Provincial Zone, Halifax Infirmary Summer Street Entrance - QEII

Department: CNS - Administration Emergency Dir

Type of Employment: Permanent Hourly FT (100%) x 1

Management Position

Posting Closing Date: 11-Nov-26

About the Opportunity

As part of the Integrated Acute & Episodic Care Network, the Director is responsible for taking a leading role in the planning, development and standardization of service and clinical processes and service guidelines/standards for the assigned clinical service areas which fall under the responsibility of the Network. The Director is responsible for providing direction and leadership regarding the provincial implementation of multiple NS Health clinical programs and initiatives that support operational improvement of clinical and core service functions.

Ongoing strategic planning is conducted in collaboration with system partners, alongside the design, management, and operational oversight of sponsored provincial policy, planning, and implementation support functions and processes. This includes policy and standards development, transition management, financial and operational oversight of transformation initiatives, program and operational performance tracking and reporting, and decision support through information management and analysis. The role is also responsible for overseeing the ongoing development, effective operation, and delivery of multiple service design strategies, programs, and initiatives.

Accountability extends to ensuring the quality and production of regular operational reports, quarterly progress and performance reports, briefing notes and briefing books, the Annual Provincial Plan, research and analysis, provincial policy, process, KPI, and target recommendations, as well as strategic project implementation plans. In addition, the role is responsible for the management of budgets and network operations, oversight of transformation-related budgets, provincial information and data measurement and reporting for strategic projects and policy implementation efforts, and the administration of multiple service provider contracts supporting
strategic initiatives and subcontracted services.

About You

We would love to hear from you if you have the following:

Master’s Degree in a health-related discipline, health administration, business administration or related subject
Eligible for registration with relevant health discipline/college or association
Certified Health Executive designation considered an asset
7-10 years of relevant leadership experience with progressive accountabilities for strategy, planning and quality management within the program area
Excellent leadership, relationship building, organizational and decision skills in support of patient, family and client centred services
Excellent coaching and mentorship skills
Strategic planning and systems thinking
Ability to build and maintain collaborative working relationships and partnerships with stakeholders
Expertise in operational and financial planning
Understands the principles of project management and demonstrated ability to create and lead complex work teams
Strong presentation and public speaking skills that are responsive to audience needs
Demonstrated advanced communications skills/positive energetic public persona
Collaboration, negotiation and persuasion skills are paramount as this role requires the engagement of internal and external stakeholders
Ability to analyze and interpret statistical data and monitor quality and performance indicators and benchmarks
Possesses a sound knowledge of management and a working knowledge of information systems
Competencies in other languages an asset, French preferred

Please ensure your resume is up to date and includes all relevant education, experience, training, and certifications.

Hours

Permanent full-time position; 75 hours biweekly

Compensation and Benefits

Pay Scale Type: Management
Band: MGT8
Hourly Rate: $67.23 - 82.35 hourly
Annual Salary: $131,089 - 160,585 annually

Successful candidates may be eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, which includes health, dental, and travel insurance; long-term disability and life insurance coverage; and a defined benefit pension plan. Additional wellness, development and employee support programs may also be available.

What you'll love about Nova Scotia Health

Nova Scotia Health is more than the province's largest provider of health services; we're a team driven by excellence in health, healing and learning. Across hospitals, health centres and community programs, our people deliver innovative, high-quality care that impacts lives across Nova Scotia and Atlantic Canada.

From vibrant city life to scenic coastal communities, Nova Scotia offers a lifestyle as rewarding as the work itself. At Nova Scotia Health, you'll find meaningful career opportunities, supportive teams and the work-life balance to enjoy everything our beautiful province has to offer. Join us and discover why so many people are choosing to call Nova Scotia home.

Once You've Applied

Thank you for your interest in this position. Only those applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Nova Scotia Health is committed to being a workforce that is free of discrimination, values diversity, and is representative, at all job levels, of the people we serve. We encourage all qualified applicants who self-identify as Indigenous, Black/African Nova Scotian, Persons of Colour, Foreign Nationals/Newcomers, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ to apply and self-identify.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Organization: Cambridge Memorial Hospital
Position: Director, Finance
Location: Cambridge, ON (on-site)
Salary: $155,000 - $185,000

THE ORGANIZATION
Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH) is more than a hospital: they are a cornerstone of a vibrant, rapidly growing community and an organization in transformation. Following a major redevelopment and expansion, CMH is redefining what exceptional community healthcare looks like, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while building for the future. CMH is building healthier communities together . As a thriving acute care hospital serving the Waterloo Wellington Region and beyond, CMH provides comprehensive services including Emergency, Surgery, Medicine, Women’s and Children’s Health, Intensive Care, and Mental Health.

As healthcare continues to evolve, CMH is seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking Director, Finance to join our senior leadership team. This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy at an organization that combines the complexity of a large healthcare environment with the agility, collegiality, and impact of a community hospital.

As healthcare funding models evolve and system pressures increase, CMH is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Director, Finance to play a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability and operational excellence. This is a high-impact opportunity to serve as a trusted financial advisor to the Executive Team and Board Committees while leading a dedicated finance team in delivering robust financial stewardship in a complex healthcare environment

THE OPPORTUNITY
Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer the Director, Finance provides enterprise-wide leadership and oversight of the hospital’s financial operations, planning, reporting, treasury, and internal control environment.
Working at the intersection of finance, operations, and strategy, the Director will help guide the organization through evolving funding models, growth opportunities, capital investments, and system transformation initiatives.

The Director is responsible for advancing financial strategy, strengthening fiscal stewardship, optimizing funding opportunities, and ensuring regulatory compliance, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As a key leader, the Director partners closely with clinical and operational leaders to align financial planning with organizational priorities. This role extends far beyond traditional financial oversight.

The Director is a trusted advisor and business partner who helps shape organizational strategy, supports critical decision-making, identifies opportunities for innovation and efficiency, and ensures CMH remains well-positioned to thrive in an increasingly complex healthcare environment.

As Director, Finance, you will drive strategic decision-making through:
Providing financial leadership and insight to the Executive Team, Directors' Council, and Board Committees, ensuring leaders have the information and analysis needed to make confident, informed decisions.
Leading long-range financial planning, capital planning, and sustainability strategies that support CMH's vision for growth and excellence.
Navigating evolving provincial funding models and healthcare priorities while identifying opportunities to optimize resources and strengthen organizational performance.
Developing and mentoring an engaged, talented finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Collaborating closely with clinical and operational leaders, the CMH Foundation, and community partners to support strategic initiatives, business cases, capital investments, and service enhancements.

IDEAL CANDIDATE
A senior leader with passion for healthcare and community impact.
Strong experience in hospitals with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive financial experience navigating complexity and driving meaningful change.
Experience working within a publicly funded environment and familiarity with Ministry of Health reporting requirements.
Proven success leading budgeting, forecasting, audit, and financial reporting functions.
Experience presenting financial information to senior leadership and/or Board Committees.
The ability to think strategically with strong business and financial acumen while maintaining operational excellence.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and a collaborative leadership style that inspires confidence and trust and an ability to engage across disciplines.
Clear, confident communicator capable of translating complex financial information for diverse audiences.
Ability to lead effectively in a dynamic and evolving healthcare environment and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills.
Advanced knowledge of MIS guidelines, systems implementations, financial systems, financial modelling and advanced spreadsheet applications.
Familiarity with procurement practices and the Broader Public Sector Procurement Directive is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business, Finance, or related field.
Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).

The Director, Finance role is a current existing vacancy. LHH Knightsbridge does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, or select applicants for a position.

CMH Inclusion Statement

At Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH), community matters to us. We acknowledge and are grateful for the opportunity to meet, work and offer healthcare on what is the traditional territories for the Anishinaabe, the Haudenosaunee and the Chinnonton.

We are committed to providing and fostering a respectful, caring, and inclusive workplace; one that generates belonging. We want a work culture where people are free to express their authentic selves and are able to bring their best daily. That includes a workplace that is free from violence, harassment and discrimination of any kind.

We welcome all applicants and encourage members of equity-deserving groups including Indigenous and LGBTQ2SIA+ communities regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, neurodiversity or physical ability. We promise to ask if needed, and to provide reasonable accommodation to you during the recruitment and selection process to ensure an equitable experience.

To support all of us in this journey, Cambridge Memorial Hospital is an employee partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity & Inclusion (CCDI) and provides access to all CMH members to CCDI resources and education. We encourage you to reflect upon our inclusive commitment to you as we welcome and encourage you to explore a promising future career at CMH.

jobs.title: Vice President (Head) of Finance
jobs.description:
Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven not-for-profit organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Organization: Cambridge Memorial Hospital
Position: Director, Finance
Location: Cambridge, ON (on-site)
Salary: $155,000 - $185,000

THE ORGANIZATION
Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH) is more than a hospital: they are a cornerstone of a vibrant, rapidly growing community and an organization in transformation. Following a major redevelopment and expansion, CMH is redefining what exceptional community healthcare looks like, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while building for the future. CMH is building healthier communities together . As a thriving acute care hospital serving the Waterloo Wellington Region and beyond, CMH provides comprehensive services including Emergency, Surgery, Medicine, Women’s and Children’s Health, Intensive Care, and Mental Health.

As healthcare continues to evolve, CMH is seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking Director, Finance to join our senior leadership team. This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy at an organization that combines the complexity of a large healthcare environment with the agility, collegiality, and impact of a community hospital.

As healthcare funding models evolve and system pressures increase, CMH is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Director, Finance to play a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability and operational excellence. This is a high-impact opportunity to serve as a trusted financial advisor to the Executive Team and Board Committees while leading a dedicated finance team in delivering robust financial stewardship in a complex healthcare environment

THE OPPORTUNITY
Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer the Director, Finance provides enterprise-wide leadership and oversight of the hospital’s financial operations, planning, reporting, treasury, and internal control environment.
Working at the intersection of finance, operations, and strategy, the Director will help guide the organization through evolving funding models, growth opportunities, capital investments, and system transformation initiatives.

The Director is responsible for advancing financial strategy, strengthening fiscal stewardship, optimizing funding opportunities, and ensuring regulatory compliance, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As a key leader, the Director partners closely with clinical and operational leaders to align financial planning with organizational priorities. This role extends far beyond traditional financial oversight.

The Director is a trusted advisor and business partner who helps shape organizational strategy, supports critical decision-making, identifies opportunities for innovation and efficiency, and ensures CMH remains well-positioned to thrive in an increasingly complex healthcare environment.

As Director, Finance, you will drive strategic decision-making through:
Providing financial leadership and insight to the Executive Team, Directors' Council, and Board Committees, ensuring leaders have the information and analysis needed to make confident, informed decisions.
Leading long-range financial planning, capital planning, and sustainability strategies that support CMH's vision for growth and excellence.
Navigating evolving provincial funding models and healthcare priorities while identifying opportunities to optimize resources and strengthen organizational performance.
Developing and mentoring an engaged, talented finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Collaborating closely with clinical and operational leaders, the CMH Foundation, and community partners to support strategic initiatives, business cases, capital investments, and service enhancements.

IDEAL CANDIDATE
A senior leader with passion for healthcare and community impact.
Strong experience in hospitals with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive financial experience navigating complexity and driving meaningful change.
Experience working within a publicly funded environment and familiarity with Ministry of Health reporting requirements.
Proven success leading budgeting, forecasting, audit, and financial reporting functions.
Experience presenting financial information to senior leadership and/or Board Committees.
The ability to think strategically with strong business and financial acumen while maintaining operational excellence.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and a collaborative leadership style that inspires confidence and trust and an ability to engage across disciplines.
Clear, confident communicator capable of translating complex financial information for diverse audiences.
Ability to lead effectively in a dynamic and evolving healthcare environment and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills.
Advanced knowledge of MIS guidelines, systems implementations, financial systems, financial modelling and advanced spreadsheet applications.
Familiarity with procurement practices and the Broader Public Sector Procurement Directive is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business, Finance, or related field.
Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).

The Director, Finance role is a current existing vacancy. LHH Knightsbridge does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, or select applicants for a position.

CMH Inclusion Statement

At Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH), community matters to us. We acknowledge and are grateful for the opportunity to meet, work and offer healthcare on what is the traditional territories for the Anishinaabe, the Haudenosaunee and the Chinnonton.

We are committed to providing and fostering a respectful, caring, and inclusive workplace; one that generates belonging. We want a work culture where people are free to express their authentic selves and are able to bring their best daily. That includes a workplace that is free from violence, harassment and discrimination of any kind.

We welcome all applicants and encourage members of equity-deserving groups including Indigenous and LGBTQ2SIA+ communities regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, neurodiversity or physical ability. We promise to ask if needed, and to provide reasonable accommodation to you during the recruitment and selection process to ensure an equitable experience.

To support all of us in this journey, Cambridge Memorial Hospital is an employee partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity & Inclusion (CCDI) and provides access to all CMH members to CCDI resources and education. We encourage you to reflect upon our inclusive commitment to you as we welcome and encourage you to explore a promising future career at CMH.
